item.title: TASS (Russian state media): China warmly welcomes Putin to APEC summit in Shenzhen — ambassador to Russia
item.description: According to Zhang Hanhui, Beijing is convinced that a meeting between the Russian leader and Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the summit will give a powerful new impetus to the steady development of relations between the two countries

item.title: Meduza: The final toll from Russia’s bombing of an aid site in the Zaporizhzhia region village of Komyshuvakha is 72. Only the Mariupol drama theater strike is believed to have killed more.
item.description: Search and rescue work has ended in the village of Komyshuvakha, in Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia region, after a Russian strike on a humanitarian aid distribution point on November 2. The death toll from the strike has risen to 72, Ukrainian Interior Minister Ivan Vyhivskyi said.

item.title: TASS (Russian state media): Russian president begins busy three-day visit to Shenzhen
item.description: Vladimir Putin has attended APEC events in various formats, including via video link, since becoming president, but this will be his first in-person participation since 2017

item.title: Meduza: Putin invokes a law countering ‘unfriendly’ countries to seize dead Russians’ unclaimed cash and gold
item.description: In early November, Vladimir Putin issued a decree titled “On certain aspects of the transfer of heirless property into the ownership of the Russian Federation.” It establishes a process for the state to seize bank savings belonging to deceased Russians for whom no heirs have been found.

item.description: Dmitry Peskov noted that there will be bilateral meetings and a separate trilateral meeting involving Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping and US leader Donald Trump

item.title: Meduza: In 1959, Nikita Khrushchev and Richard Nixon held one of the Cold War’s defining conversations: the ‘Kitchen Debate,’ inside a model American house at a Moscow exhibition
item.description: In 1959, one of the most significant events of the Khrushchev Thaw took place in Moscow’s Sokolniki Park: the American National Exhibition. In its pavilions, Soviet citizens could explore American art and see how Americans lived: what cars they drove, what kitchens they cooked in, and what beds they slept in. But what the exhibition in Sokolniki is remembered for most is not its works of art and design, but the “Kitchen Debate.” On July 24, U.S. Vice President Richard Nixon arrived for the…

item.description: The Russian leader emphasized that the participation of the Korean People’s Army military units in liberating the territory of the Kursk Region has become a new chapter in the history of countries’ military camaraderie

item.title: Meduza: Russian publisher cuts Pushkin’s drinking stanza from third-grade textbook, citing anti-alcohol law. The Education Ministry’s response? Don’t do that — it’s Pushkin.
item.description: The news outlet Fontanka reported that a third-grade textbook, “Literaturnoye chteniye” (“Literary Reading”), published by Prosveshcheniye in 2023, includes an abridged version of Alexander Pushkin’s poem “Zimny vecher” (“Winter Evening”), known for its opening line, “The storm shrouds the sky in darkness.” The stanza in which the speaker suggests that his nanny join him in drinking “to drown our sorrows” was cut. The omission prompted a wave of mockery and outrage online, forcing the publisher…

item.title: Meduza: Decorated Russian actor Alexander Goncharuk accused of grooming underage students
item.description: Several female graduates of the Omsk College of Music and Education have accused Alexander Goncharuk, 63, of grooming and sexually harassing minors. Goncharuk is a teacher, an actor at the Omsk Drama Theater, and a recipient of the honorary title People’s Artist of Russia. On November 15, the Omsk news outlet Gorod 55 reported, citing its sources, that Goncharuk had submitted his resignation from the college. His former students have contacted Russia’s Investigative Committee. The agency has…

item.title: Meduza: EU sanctions Russia’s biggest oil refineries, payment service YooMoney, and more than 40 banks
item.description: The European Union has expanded its sanctions list targeting Russia to include oil refineries, petrochemical plants and companies, and dozens of banks. The EU published the sanctions document in its Official Journal.

item.title: TASS (Russian state media): Cuba asks Russia, allies to 'stay on our side' amid US threats — ambassador
item.description: Cuban Ambassador to Russia Enrique Orta Gonzalez recalled that over the past nine months, his country has been facing "an unprecedented US aggression, the tightening economic, trade, and financial blockade, as well as energy and naval blockade"
